nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, let $k$ and $n$ be natural numbers, and let $A$ be a $k \times k$ matrix over $R$ with rows and columns indexed by $\{0, \dots, k-1\}$, viewed as the weighted adjacency matrix of a weighted digraph on these $k$ vertices. Then for all vertices $i$ and $j$,
nodes.title: Powers of a weighted adjacency matrix sum the weights of walks

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$, the Andrásfai graph is the Cayley graph of the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}/(3k+2)\mathbb{Z}$ whose connection set $C$ consists of the residues whose representative in $\{0, 1, \dots, 3k+1\}$ is congruent to $1$ modulo $3$: two distinct residues $x$ and $y$ are adjacent when $y - x \in C$ or $x - y \in C$.
nodes.title: Andrásfai graph

nodes.summary: Entry `(v, j)` is `σ j` if `b j = v` and `0` otherwise.
nodes.title: Entries of the boundary-column matrix

nodes.summary: The real `V × F` matrix whose column `j` is `σ j` times the standard basis vector at the anchor `b j`.
nodes.title: Boundary columns

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 2$, the complete graph on $n$ vertices has exactly $n^{n-2}$ spanning trees.
nodes.title: Cayley's formula

nodes.summary: The Coxeter graph is the simple graph whose $28$ vertices are the pairs $(i, j)$ with $i \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$ and $j \in \mathbb{Z}/7\mathbb{Z}$, and whose edges are the following: for each $i \in \{1, 2, 3\}$, the vertices $(i, j)$ and $(i, j')$ are adjacent when $j - j' = i$ or $j' - j = i$ in $\mathbb{Z}/7\mathbb{Z}$, and for each $j$ the vertex $(0, j)$ is adjacent to $(1, j)$, $(2, j)$ and $(3, j)$. There are…
nodes.title: Coxeter graph

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a set with a binary operation written as multiplication, and let $C \subseteq G$. The *Cayley digraph* $X(G, C)$ is the directed graph whose vertices are the elements of $G$, with an arc $u \to v$ exactly when $v = uc$ for some $c \in C$.
nodes.title: Cayley digraph

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $T$ be a set of permutations of $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$, typically a set of transpositions in the symmetric group $S_n$. The edge-transposition graph of $T$ is the simple graph with vertex set $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ in which two distinct vertices $i$ and $j$ are adjacent if and only if the transposition swapping $i$ and $j$ belongs to $T$.
nodes.title: Edge-transposition graph

nodes.summary: Every finite group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of a finite simple graph.
nodes.title: Frucht's theorem

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set and let $d$ be a natural number. Then $G$ is a Moore graph of diameter $d$ when $G$ has diameter $d$ and girth $2d + 1$.
nodes.title: Moore graph

nodes.summary: For a loopless finite multigraph, a real vector `r` lies in the range of `orientedIncidence end₁ end₂` if and only if its sum over the vertices of every connected component of `underlyingGraph end₁ end₂` vanishes.
nodes.title: Range of the oriented incidence matrix

nodes.summary: If the endpoints of `e` are distinct, the entry of `orientedIncidence end₁ end₂` at `(end₂ e, e)` is `-1`.
nodes.title: Second-endpoint entry

nodes.summary: If the endpoints of `e` are distinct, the entry of `orientedIncidence end₁ end₂` at `(end₁ e, e)` is `1`.
nodes.title: First-endpoint entry

nodes.summary: The column of `e` vanishes at every vertex other than `end₁ e` and `end₂ e`.
nodes.title: Entries away from the endpoints

nodes.summary: Entry `(v, e)` is `[end₁ e = v] - [end₂ e = v]`.
nodes.title: Entries of the oriented incidence matrix

nodes.summary: The real `V × E` matrix of the multigraph with endpoint maps `end₁ end₂`: column `e` is `+1` at `end₁ e` and `-1` at `end₂ e`. Distinct edges, including parallel ones, give distinct columns.
nodes.title: Oriented incidence matrix of a multigraph

nodes.summary: The Petersen graph is the generalized Johnson graph $J(5,2,0)$: its vertices are the $2$-element subsets of $\{0, 1, 2, 3, 4\}$, and two of them are adjacent exactly when they are disjoint.
nodes.title: Petersen graph

nodes.summary: For a loopless finite multigraph, the rank of its real oriented incidence matrix plus the number of connected components of `underlyingGraph end₁ end₂` equals the number of vertices.
nodes.title: Incidence rank plus number of components

nodes.summary: For a loopless finite multigraph, the rank of its real oriented incidence matrix is the number of vertices minus the number of connected components of `underlyingGraph end₁ end₂`.
nodes.title: Rank of the oriented incidence matrix

nodes.summary: For a loopless finite multigraph and finitely many boundary columns `σ j • e_{b j}` with every `σ j = ±1`, the real matrix obtained by adjoining them to the oriented incidence matrix is surjective if and only if every connected component of `underlyingGraph end₁ end₂` contains the anchor `b j` of some boundary column. The components are those of the interior edges alone.
nodes.title: Surjectivity with free boundary columns

nodes.summary: An edge whose endpoints are distinct makes them adjacent in `underlyingGraph end₁ end₂`.
nodes.title: An edge joins its endpoints in the underlying graph

nodes.summary: Vertices `u` and `v` are adjacent in `underlyingGraph end₁ end₂` if and only if they are distinct and some edge joins them, in either orientation.
nodes.title: Adjacency in the underlying graph

nodes.summary: Reachability in `underlyingGraph end₁ end₂` is reachability through edges of the multigraph, `Relation.ReflTransGen` of `AdjacentUsing` on all edges.
nodes.title: Reachability in the underlying graph

nodes.summary: For endpoint maps `end₁ end₂ : E → V`, the simple graph on `V` in which distinct vertices are adjacent when some edge joins them. It forgets multiplicities and loops and is used only for connectivity.
nodes.title: Underlying simple graph of a multigraph

nodes.summary: Entry `j` of `x ᵥ* boundaryColumns b σ` is `x (b j) * σ j`.
nodes.title: Row vector times the boundary columns

nodes.summary: Entry `e` of `x ᵥ* orientedIncidence end₁ end₂` is the difference `x (end₁ e) - x (end₂ e)` across `e`.
nodes.title: Row vector times the oriented incidence matrix

nodes.summary: For a loopless multigraph with finitely many vertices, a real vector `x` satisfies `x ᵥ* orientedIncidence end₁ end₂ = 0` if and only if `x` is constant on each connected component of `underlyingGraph end₁ end₂`.
nodes.title: Left kernel of the oriented incidence matrix

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
